transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m here because... I just keep snapping at people. It's getting to be a real problem at work. Like at this safety meeting we had recently, I just started yelling before I could even stop myself. And now the younger inspectors on the floor, they act scared to even ask me anything. I just need to figure out how to get it under control.
Between these moments when you lose your temper, how is your overall mood?

I'm not really sure. I haven't paid much attention to it, to be honest. I just sort of... go to work, do my inspections, and come home. I haven't really stopped to think about what my actual mood is like when I'm not getting mad at people.
About how often are you having these angry outbursts?

I'm not exactly sure. I haven't really been keeping count of them or anything. It just... it happens enough that it's causing problems, like I said, but I couldn't give you a specific number or tell you exactly how many times a week it is.
During these outbursts, have you ever broken things or become physically aggressive toward anyone?

No, I haven't ever hit anyone or broken anything. Like I mentioned earlier, it's really just the yelling. I just... snap at people. Like at that safety meeting, I just started shouting before I even realized I was doing it. I guess my voice gets pretty loud and harsh, which is why those younger inspectors act so scared to ask me questions now. But no, it's never gotten physical.
About how long have you been experiencing these outbursts of yelling and snapping?
Well, it's been going on since that machinery accident... the one that happened right after the overnight schedule change. So, looking at the calendar, it's been about two years and four months now.
Did you hit your head or lose consciousness during that machinery accident?
No, I didn't hit my head. I was awake the whole time, so... no, I didn't pass out or lose consciousness or anything like that.
Do you find yourself having unwanted memories or nightmares about the machinery accident?

Yes, I do. It doesn't even take much to bring it up, either. Just... hearing a loud clank from a cart, or catching the smell of hot oil, it can put me right back in that bay. I'll just see my coworker standing by the machine, exactly like it's happening in front of me all over again.

latest_inference.note: Confirmed re-experiencing symptoms (intrusive memories, flashbacks, sensory triggers) dating back to a workplace trauma over 2 years ago, which along with irritability/hyperarousal confirms PTSD and rules out IED (F63.81), MDD (F32), and GAD (F41.1).
